title: Lane reservation and spot eviction policy for plan classes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During regional load spikes and quota exhaustion we observe severe unfairness across plan classes: free plan traffic can cause tail latency for paid customers, while paid traffic can be completely blocked when enterprise reserved headroom is consumed by bursts. Current admission controller is strictly first-come and misses opportunities for graceful degradation.

Goal: Implement a lane reservation + spot eviction policy that: 1) guarantees a configurable minimum headroom for enterprise and paid lanes, 2) allows best-effort 'spot' admission for lower tiers that can be evicted mid-request or on admission when higher-priority credits are needed, 3) supports borrowing and time-decay to smooth short-term spikes, and 4) automatically falls back to cheaper/quantized model variants when capacity is constrained.

Design proposal (high level):
- Per-plan lane constructs: RESERVED, GUARDED, SPOT. RESERVED holds hard headroom for enterprise; GUARDED is soft-protected for paid customers; SPOT accepts free/burst traffic subject to eviction.
- Credit accounting: token-bucket per account + per-lane aggregate buckets with replenishment rates tied to plan quotas. Borrowing: SPOT can borrow from GUARDED up to a configurable fraction; borrowed amount decays over a warmup window to avoid sustained bleed.
- Admission flow changes: request -> tenant resolution -> regional affinity check -> lane scoring. Lane scoring considers credit balance, SLO risk (current p95/p99 vs target), and model cost. If admitted to SPOT, annotate request for eviction eligibility and degraded-mode flag (e.g., quantized_model variant).
- Eviction policy: pre-emit eviction advisory prior to admission when GUARDED credits dip below threshold. If eviction required, pick SPOT requests to preempt based on oldest-founded credit usage and lowest SLA score. Eviction can occur at admission (reject) or mid-request (attempt graceful abort / cached-response or fallback model).
- Model variant fallbacks: map expensive model variants (fp16/large-context) -> lighter quantized variants that preserve response correctness for many classes of requests. Routing table includes compatibility constraints so fallback is safe.
- Regional selection: favor local region if lane has headroom; otherwise route to nearest region with available GUARDED capacity. Prefer avoid cross-region if data residency prohibits.

Trade-offs and mitigations:
- Mid-request eviction can harm UX; mitigate by preferring admission-time rejection first and using aborts only when response latency budget is exceeded. Provide per-tenant telemetry to show evictions and credit usage.
- Borrowing risks starvation when warm-up window misconfigured; add adaptive decay based on sustained delta and circuit-breaker to stop borrowing after repeated breaches.

Rollout plan:
1) Simulate (in e2e traffic simulator using historical traces) and verify fairness metrics.
2) Implement feature-flagged admission controller changes behind 'lane_reservation_v1'.
3) Canary in one low-traffic region with paid and enterprise test tenants; measure p95/p99, served_tokens_per_tier, eviction_rate.
4) Gradual rollout with 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% of hosts with kill-switch.

Metrics and success criteria:
- p99 latency for enterprise remains <= baseline + 10% during peak.
- Fraction of paid-tier requests served (availability) >= 99.5% under target load.
- Eviction rate < 0.5% requests for SPOT during steady load; spike-friendly borrowing prevents cascades.
- Fairness ratio (served_tokens_per_credit per-tier) moves toward target band within 24h of rollout.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for lane scoring and credit accounting.
- Load tests with synthetic bursts to validate borrowing/decay.
- Chaos test: intentionally saturate GUARDED and ensure SPOT eviction behaves as expected.
- Regression tests for model-compatibility when routing to quantized fallbacks.

Implementation notes (engineering):
- Admission controller changes primarily in router service (rust/gRPC layer). Add per-tenant stats in metrics bridge and expose debug API for current lane allocations.
- Small datastore addition: per-lane aggregate counters in redis; keep operations idempotent.
- UI: Console needs a per-tenant dashboard showing reserved headroom, current borrow level, and eviction events (follow-up ticket in product).

Links to artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Lane+Reservation+Design
- Simulation harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sim/pull/412
- Prototype router branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/tree/feature/lane-reservation-v1

Open questions:
- Exact % reserve for enterprise vs paid (propose enterprise 20%, paid 30% guarded, remainder spot but tunable).
- Should mid-request eviction return a partial result or a structured fallback error? (Ops prefers structured fallback).
- Legal/data-residency constraints for cross-region fallbacks — need input from compliance on default behavior.
